summary: Billing gap: missing provisional buffer credit after partial postback ACK truncation during bulk embedding job
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a missing provisional buffer credit on the finalized invoice after running a large bulk embedding job. The job triggered a burst of postbacks; some postback acknowledgements were truncated by an intermediate proxy, leading to partial ingestion and missing provisional buffer allocation. Impact: CloudAtlas is seeing a ~12% delta between expected provisional credit and billed usage on the finalized invoice for the billing period. This could lead to a charge that the customer disputes and potential SLA escalation.

Environment: Dedicated deployment for CloudAtlas in us-east-1. Bulk embedding job submitted via API key attached to a reserved dedicated cluster.

Observed behavior: Bulk job ran at 2026-03-04T21:30Z. Postback spikes between 21:31–21:45Z. Postback-collector logs show repeated TCP resets and truncated ACKs from an edge proxy. Some postbacks were accepted but not fully acknowledged, resulting in acceptance without completed postback payloads in the billing reconciler. As a result the provisional buffer credit that should have been reserved during the hour was not applied; billing aggregation missed the buffer window.

Expected behavior: Partial or retried postbacks should be deduplicated and the provisional buffer credit should be applied conservatively when a postback is accepted for at least one shard. Finalized invoice should align with provisional credits recorded during the hour.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer starts a large batch embedding job (bulk size ~120k vectors) using dedicated cluster in us-east-1.
2) Artificially inject a short-lived proxy-induced TCP reset on the postback ingestion path to mimic intermediate proxy overload (~15 minutes).
3) Observe postback-collector logs and billing provisional buffer allocations for the hour.
4) Compare provisional buffer credit lines with finalized invoice after reconciliation run.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Opened ticket after CloudAtlas rep (tara@cloudatlas) reported missing provisional buffer credit on finalized invoice for period ending 2026-03-05. Customer provided job id and a small redacted screenshot of invoice diff.
2026-03-10 - Support triage (Liam Chen): Confirmed customer tier is dedicated and that they had burst capacity. Assigned to billing-engineering for investigation. Added label 'postback'.

2026-03-11 - Billing eng (Sofia Ramos): Initial hypothesis: partial postback ACKs accepted by postback-collector but truncated before payload stored in S3-backed queue, causing billing aggregator to mark postback as acknowledged without payload size metadata. Looking into postback-collector metrics and proxy logs in #support-billing slack.
2026-03-11 - SRE (Marcus Lee): Found 503 spike on edge-proxy between 21:31–21:38Z. Duplicate connections and half-closed sockets observed. Filed infra alert INF-2026-0311-EDGE for follow-up.
2026-03-12 - Support (Liam Chen): Reached out to customer with temporary reconciliation numbers and asked for permission to run a small probe job to reproduce. Customer approved (tara@cloudatlas).
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Edge proxy truncation caused postback-collector to create acceptance records lacking payload metrics, so billing aggregator applied no provisional credit.
Action: correlate collector acceptance events with S3 payload write confirmations.

Hypothesis 2: Billing reconciler has an ordering assumption: when acceptance event arrives but payload write confirmation is delayed/absent, reconciler skips provisional credit.
Action: review billing-aggregator commit window (billing-aggregator/commit_window.go) and add logging to capture acceptance-without-payload events. Linked PR created.

Findings: Found ~3.2k acceptance events for pf_* ids with no corresponding s3_put events for the hour. Edge proxy (NLB) returned RSTs; postback-collector marked some postbacks as 'accepted' pre-write. Confirmed mismatch with billing-aggregator logs showing provisional_applied=FALSE. Evidence in dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pmQKX/postback-ingestion?orgId=1&from=2026-03-04T21:00:00Z&to=2026-03-04T22:00:00Z
Temporary mitigation tested: Re-run of the small probe job produced postbacks successfully and provisional buffer credited when proxy behaved normally.
resolution: Short-term workaround: Manually apply provisional buffer credit for the affected hour to CloudAtlas account and issue a credit memo for the delta of 149.32 tokens equivalent. Finance notified and provisional credit applied to account ledger on 2026-03-12. (see FIN-CR-2026-045)

Medium-term fix: Billing-aggregator change to treat acceptance events without payload write confirmation as 'pending' not 'skipped'. New logic added to billing-aggregator to hold provisional allocation for 10 minutes awaiting payload confirmation; if absent, mark as failed and surface for reconciliation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-aggregator/pull/212 merged to main on 2026-03-11, deployed to prod canary 2026-03-12.
Infrastructure follow-up: Edge proxy NLB configuration updated to increase idle timeout and connection retry thresholds. Infra ticket INF-2026-0311-EDGE tracks changes.

Post-incident actions: 1) Add an alert to detect acceptance-without-payload rate > 0.5% in any 5m window. 2) Update postback runbook with step to reconcile billing provisional allocations after transient proxy errors. 3) Outreach: dedicated account manager scheduled a call with CloudAtlas for 2026-03-13 to confirm credits and next steps.
Status: Customer credit applied; billing logic fix merged and rolled out to canary. Monitoring alerts added. Closing pending after verification call and final invoice check on 2026-03-15.
resolution_notes: Manual credit applied and billing aggregator logic change merged. Customer notified by Liam Chen. Follow-up verification scheduled and infra ticket opened for proxy hardening.
